descripcion_es: Concession, rephrasing, giving examples and concluding.
resumen: Connectors for building an argument: conceding, contrasting, rephrasing, giving examples, adding and concluding. They are what gives cohesion to a presentation or a summary.

explicacion.texto: Pay attention to the grammar of each connector: some are followed by a clause (although, whereas), others by a noun or -ing (despite, in spite of), and others are adverbs that start a sentence and take a comma (however, nevertheless).

filas: although / even though + clause
introduces a fact that contrasts with the main idea (es: aunque / aun cuando)
Although it was late, we kept working.
despite / in spite of + noun or -ing
without being prevented by (es: a pesar de)
Despite the rain, the match went ahead.
however, / nevertheless,
but, in contrast to what was said (es: sin embargo, / no obstante,)
Prices rose. However, demand held up.
whereas / while
while on the other side (contrast) (es: mientras que)
Exports rose, whereas imports fell.
admittedly
it must be accepted that (es: hay que reconocer que)
Admittedly, the plan has some flaws.
even so
in spite of that (es: aun así)
It was expensive. Even so, we bought it.
on the other hand
looking at another aspect (es: por otro lado)
On the other hand, it would create jobs.
on the contrary
the opposite is true (denies what came before) (es: al contrario)
It isn't cheap; on the contrary, it's very expensive.
in other words
saying it differently (es: en otras palabras)
In other words, the plan failed.
that is (to say) / i.e.
more precisely, namely (es: es decir)
The core rate, that is, excluding energy, rose.
for instance / for example / e.g.
as an example (es: por ejemplo)
Some cities, for instance Bilbao, have changed a lot.
such as
like (to list examples) (es: como)
Countries such as Italy and Greece...
in particular / notably
especially, above all (es: en particular / especialmente)
Prices rose, notably in food.
moreover / furthermore / in addition
also, in addition (formal) (es: además)
Moreover, the costs are too high.
as a result / consequently
because of this (es: como resultado / en consecuencia)
As a result, the factory closed.
therefore / thus
for this reason, so (es: por lo tanto / así pues)
Therefore, we need a new approach.
in conclusion / to sum up
to finish, summing up (es: en conclusión / en resumen)
To sum up, the risks outweigh the benefits.
all in all / on the whole
considering everything (es: en general, a fin de cuentas)
All in all, it was a good year.

items: “Actually” does not mean “actualmente” but “in reality, in fact” (es: en realidad); Spanish “actualmente” is “currently” or “at present”.
“Eventually” means “finally, in the end”, not Spanish “eventualmente” (possibly, by chance).
Despite never takes “of”: say “despite the rain” or “in spite of the rain”.

ejemplos.frase: Although the plan is expensive, it will pay off in the long run.
ejemplos.traduccion: Aunque el plan es caro, saldrá rentable a largo plazo.

ejemplos.frase: Despite having little money, they travelled all over Asia.
ejemplos.traduccion: A pesar de tener poco dinero, viajaron por toda Asia.

ejemplos.frase: Some sports, such as cycling and swimming, are easy on the knees.
ejemplos.traduccion: Algunos deportes, como el ciclismo y la natación, cuidan las rodillas.

ejemplos.frase: The northern regions are growing, whereas the south is stagnating.
ejemplos.traduccion: Las regiones del norte crecen, mientras que el sur está estancado.

ejemplos.frase: The film is long. Even so, it never feels boring.
ejemplos.traduccion: La película es larga. Aun así, en ningún momento resulta aburrida.

ejemplos.frase: He actually lives in Toledo, not in Madrid.
ejemplos.traduccion: En realidad vive en Toledo, no en Madrid.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: Despite of the crisis, sales grew.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: “Despite” does not take “of”; “in spite of” does.
Spanish “actualmente” is “currently / at present”; “actually” means “in fact” (es: en realidad).

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: Although the rain, we went out.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: Despite the rain, we went out.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: “Although” needs a clause with a verb; with a noun, use “despite”.
“However” at the start of a sentence is followed by a comma.

ejercicios.frase: ___ the bad weather, the concert was a success.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule from this unit: despite is followed by a noun or -ing, and never takes of. The clue is the bad weather, a noun with no verb, and the contrast between the bad weather and the success. That is why only Despite works.
ejercicios.traduccion: A pesar del mal tiempo, el concierto fue un éxito.

por_opcion.Despite: Correct: “in spite of”, followed by a noun and without of.
por_opcion.Although: Incorrect: although needs a clause with a verb (although the weather was bad).
por_opcion.Despite of: Incorrect: this is the typical mistake in this unit; despite never takes of.
por_opcion.However: Incorrect: however is an adverb that starts a sentence with a comma; it cannot be followed by a noun.

glosario.definicion_l: lack of respect accompanied by a feeling of intense dislike · contemptuous disregard

ejercicios.frase: ___ she was tired, she finished the report.
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the other half of the rule: although is followed by a clause with a subject and a verb. The clue is she was tired, a complete clause. Despite and in spite of would need a noun or -ing (despite being tired), and nevertheless would come after the clause stating the obstacle.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Before a clause with a verb, use “although”.
ejercicios.traduccion: Aunque estaba cansada, terminó el informe.

por_opcion.Although: Correct: “even if it is true that”, followed by a clause with a verb.
por_opcion.Despite: Incorrect: it cannot go with a clause; you would have to say despite being tired.
por_opcion.In spite of: Incorrect: like despite, it needs a noun or -ing.
por_opcion.Nevertheless: Incorrect: “however”; it is an adverb that introduces what happens in spite of the obstacle, not the obstacle itself.

glosario.definicion_l: a written document describing the findings of some individual or group · the act of informing by verbal report

ejercicios.frase: Despite of the strike, the trains ran normally.
respuestas: Despite the strike, the trains ran normally.
In spite of the strike, the trains ran normally.
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the first mistake listed in this unit: despite does not take of; in spite of does. The clue is “Despite of”, a copy of Spanish “a pesar de”. Correct it by removing of or by using the other expression, in spite of.
ejercicios.traduccion: A pesar de la huelga, los trenes circularon con normalidad.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Despite of the strike, the trains ran normally.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: despite never takes of.

errores_previstos.respuesta: In spite the strike, the trains ran normally.
errores_previstos.explicacion: In spite needs of: in spite of the strike.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Although the strike, the trains ran normally.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Although needs a clause with a verb, not a noun.

glosario.definicion_l: a group's refusal to work in protest against low pay or bad work conditions · an attack that is intended to seize or inflict damage on or destroy an objective

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with a two-word connector (giving an example).
ejercicios.frase: Some fruits, for ___, oranges and kiwis, are rich in vitamin C.
ejercicios.explicacion: It is for instance or for example, from the second table. The clue is for before the gap and the list of two fruits between commas. The two expressions are equivalent, so both are accepted; for instance is slightly more formal.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “For instance” or “for example” = es: por ejemplo.
ejercicios.traduccion: Algunas frutas, por ejemplo las naranjas y los kiwis, son ricas en vitamina C.

errores_previstos.explicacion: French or copied spelling; in English it is example.
For such does not exist; such goes with as (such as) and without for.

ejercicios.frase: Madrid has grown a lot, ___ many rural areas have lost population.
ejercicios.explicacion: It is whereas, “while on the other side”, from the first table: it contrasts two opposite facts in a single sentence. The clue is the opposition between growing and losing population, and that what follows is a complete clause. Therefore and moreover would start a sentence with a comma, and despite would need a noun.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Whereas” expresses a contrast between two facts.
ejercicios.traduccion: Madrid ha crecido mucho, mientras que muchas zonas rurales han perdido población.

por_opcion.whereas: Correct: it contrasts two facts and is followed by a clause.
por_opcion.therefore: Incorrect: it shows a consequence; depopulation is not presented as an effect of Madrid's growth.
por_opcion.moreover: Incorrect: it adds something in the same direction, not a contrast.
por_opcion.despite: Incorrect: it needs a noun or -ing, not a clause.

glosario.definicion_l: an area outside of cities and towns

ejercicios.frase: Actually, she works as a teacher in Murcia, but before she was a nurse.
respuestas: Currently, she works as a teacher in Murcia, but before she was a nurse.
At present, she works as a teacher in Murcia, but before she was a nurse.
Now, she works as a teacher in Murcia, but before she was a nurse.
At the moment, she works as a teacher in Murcia, but before she was a nurse.
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the false friend from the list in this unit: actually means “in fact”, not Spanish “actualmente”. The clue is the time contrast with before she was a nurse, which needs an adverb of present time. Use currently, at present, at the moment or now; all are accepted.
ejercicios.traduccion: Actualmente trabaja como profesora en Murcia, pero antes era enfermera.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Actually, she works as a teacher in Murcia, but before she was a nurse.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: actually means “in fact”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Actual, she works as a teacher in Murcia, but before she was a nurse.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Actual is an adjective and means “real, true”, not Spanish “actual” (current).

errores_previstos.respuesta: Eventually, she works as a teacher in Murcia, but before she was a nurse.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Eventually is another false friend: it means “in the end, after some time”, not “currently”.

glosario.definicion_l: at this time or period; now
one skilled in caring for young children or the sick (usually under the supervision of a physician) · a woman who is the custodian of children

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with one word (saying it differently).
ejercicios.frase: The project is over budget and behind schedule. In other ___, it is a failure.
ejercicios.explicacion: It is in other words, from the second table, for rephrasing. The clue is In other ___ and the fact that the sentence sums up what came before in a more direct way. The word is words, always plural in this expression.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “In other words” rephrases what has been said.
ejercicios.traduccion: El proyecto supera el presupuesto y va con retraso. En otras palabras, es un fracaso.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The fixed expression is plural: in other words.
In other terms is an unnatural copy; the expression is in other words.

ejercicios.frase: The house is not small; ___, it has six bedrooms.
ejercicios.explicacion: It is on the contrary, from the first table: it denies what came before and states the opposite. The clue is the negative sentence is not small followed by a fact that proves the opposite. On the other hand, by contrast, presents another aspect without denying the first one; this is the typical confusion.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “On the contrary” denies what came before and states the opposite.
ejercicios.traduccion: La casa no es pequeña; al contrario, tiene seis dormitorios.

por_opcion.on the contrary: Correct: it denies that it is small and states the opposite.
por_opcion.on the other hand: Incorrect: it adds another aspect, but it does not deny what came before.
por_opcion.in addition: Incorrect: “also”; it does not fit after a negative statement that is going to be refuted.
por_opcion.for instance: Incorrect: “for example”; six bedrooms is not an example of it not being small, but proof of the opposite.

glosario.definicion_l: a room used primarily for sleeping

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with a connector (expressing a consequence).
ejercicios.frase: Demand fell sharply. As a ___, the company cut production.
ejercicios.explicacion: It is as a result, from the second table, for consequence; as a consequence is equivalent and is also accepted. The clue is As a ___ and the cause-and-effect relation between the fall in demand and the cut. Both expressions start a sentence and are followed by a comma.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “As a result / as a consequence” introduces the effect.
ejercicios.traduccion: La demanda cayó bruscamente. En consecuencia, la empresa recortó la producción.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Consequently is a complete connector; after As a a noun is needed: result or consequence.
The expression is singular: as a result.

ejercicios.frase: Countries ___ Portugal and Ireland received EU assistance.
ejercicios.explicacion: It is such as, from the second table: “like”, to list examples within the sentence, without a pause. The clue is that the examples come straight after the noun countries, without commas. For instance would need commas or a different position, and like as and as such do not have this meaning.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Such as” introduces examples within the sentence.
ejercicios.traduccion: Países como Portugal e Irlanda recibieron ayuda de la UE.

por_opcion.such as: Correct: it introduces examples within the sentence, without commas.
por_opcion.for instance: Incorrect here: it would need to go between commas (Some countries, for instance Portugal, …).
por_opcion.like as: Incorrect: it does not exist; you say like or such as, but not both.
por_opcion.as such: Incorrect: it means “in itself, in the strict sense”, not “like, for example”.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with one word (meaning “in spite of that”).
ejercicios.frase: The hotel was far from the beach. Even ___, we loved it.
ejercicios.explicacion: It is even so, from the first table: it introduces something that happens in spite of what was said before. The clue is Even ___ and the contrast between a drawback and the fact that they loved the hotel. It starts a sentence and is followed by a comma, like however.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Even so” = in spite of that (es: aun así).
ejercicios.traduccion: El hotel estaba lejos de la playa. Aun así, nos encantó.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Even though means “although” and needs a clause after it; it cannot be followed by a comma like this.
Even if means “although, whether or not” and also needs a clause.

glosario.definicion_l: despite anything to the contrary (usually preceding a concession)

ejercicios.frase: The proposal is cheap and fast. ___, it is popular with voters.
ejercicios.explicacion: It is moreover, “in addition”, from the second table: it adds an argument in the same direction. The clue is that the second sentence adds another advantage to the previous ones and that the gap starts a sentence followed by a comma. Whereas, although and despite express opposition and have a different grammar.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Moreover” adds an argument in the same direction.
ejercicios.traduccion: La propuesta es barata y rápida. Además, es popular entre los votantes.

por_opcion.Moreover: Correct: it adds an argument in favour, “in addition”.
por_opcion.Whereas: Incorrect: it contrasts two facts within a sentence and is not followed by a comma.
por_opcion.Although: Incorrect: it introduces a concession, not one more advantage.
por_opcion.Despite: Incorrect: it needs a noun and expresses opposition.

glosario.definicion_l: a citizen who has a legal right to vote

ejercicios.frase: Although it was raining, they played tennis.
respuestas: Despite the rain, they played tennis.
Despite it raining, they played tennis.
Despite the fact that it was raining, they played tennis.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule for despite: it goes with a noun, with -ing or with the fact that + clause. The clause it was raining can become the noun the rain, the -ing form it raining, or stay as a clause with the fact that. All three options are correct; what you cannot do is put the clause directly after despite.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Despite” goes with a noun, -ing or “the fact that” + clause.
ejercicios.traduccion: A pesar de la lluvia, jugaron al tenis.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Despite it was raining, they played tennis.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Despite cannot be followed by a clause with a finite verb.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Despite of the rain, they played tennis.
Despite that it was raining, they played tennis.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The fact is missing: the formula is despite the fact that.

respuestas: To sum up the reform has failed
ejercicios.explicacion: It is to sum up, from the second table, for concluding: it starts the sentence and then comes the main clause, subject (the reform) + verb (has failed). The capital T in To shows that the sentence begins with it. It is a clear way to end a presentation.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “To sum up” starts the conclusion; then subject + verb + object.
ejercicios.traduccion: En resumen, la reforma ha fracasado.

errores_previstos.respuesta: To up sum the reform has failed
errores_previstos.explicacion: The fixed expression is to sum up, with up at the end.

errores_previstos.respuesta: To sum up has the reform failed
errores_previstos.explicacion: That is question word order; after the connector comes subject + verb: the reform has failed.

glosario.definicion_l: a change for the better as a result of correcting abuses · a campaign aimed to correct abuses or malpractices

ejercicios.frase: After hours of negotiation, they ___ reached an agreement.
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the false friend eventually from the list in this unit: it means “finally, after a long time”, not Spanish “eventualmente”. The clue is after hours of negotiation, which shows a result reached after a long process. Actually and occasionally are other false friends or do not fit.
ejercicios.traduccion: Tras horas de negociación, finalmente llegaron a un acuerdo.

por_opcion.eventually: Correct: finally, at the end of a long process.
por_opcion.possibly: Incorrect: “perhaps”; it does not fit with a completed fact such as reached.
por_opcion.actually: Incorrect: it means “in fact”; it does not express that the agreement came after a long time.
por_opcion.occasionally: Incorrect: “from time to time”; it makes no sense with a single agreement reached.

glosario.definicion_l: after an unspecified period of time or an especially long delay

descripcion_larga_es: Connectors for building an argument at an advanced level: conceding (admittedly, even so), contrasting (whereas, on the contrary), rephrasing (in other words, that is), giving examples (for instance, such as), adding (moreover) and concluding (to sum up, all in all). They give cohesion to a presentation, a summary or a report. Spanish speakers find the grammar of each one difficult, as well as the false friends actually and eventually.

contexto.que_es: These are the connectors typical of argument. Some are followed by a clause (although, whereas), others by a noun or -ing (despite, in spite of), and others are adverbs that start a sentence with a comma (however, nevertheless, moreover, as a result). Each one marks a specific logical relation: concession, contrast, rephrasing, example, addition, consequence or conclusion.
contexto.por_que_importa: In a B2-level oral presentation or written summary, cohesion depends on them: the examining board or the examiner follows the argument thanks to these signals. Confusing on the contrary with on the other hand, or using actually for Spanish “actualmente”, changes the meaning. They are also essential for reading the economic press and institutional reports.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: When defending a position, comparing data, summarising a text or closing a speech. The signal is the role of the sentence in the argument: whether it concedes, contrasts, clarifies, gives an example or concludes. Spanish speakers tend to overuse but and and, to say despite of and to forget the comma after however.
